title: introduce-invocation-scenario-profiling-and-spectral-cost-anchors
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds invocation scenario profiling metrics, a new spectral cost anchor sampler, Grafana dashboard panels for scenario cohorts, and tuned alerts for spectral anomaly windows. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config flag.
description:
Motivation: We routinely see noisy long-tail cost and latency signals that are hard to attribute to a small set of invocation characteristics (prompt shape, model variant, routing policy, KV cache hit pattern). Existing rollups and token histograms capture macro trends but fail to isolate correlated spectral patterns that indicate systemic regressions (e.g., a specific prompt family that triggers elevated per-token cost during particular time windows). This PR introduces an end-to-end feature set: Invocation Scenario Profiling + Spectral Cost Anchors.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight invocation "scenario" fingerprint computed at ingress which captures a compact signature of: prompt-shape bucket, caller-client, model variant tag, first-k token entropy bucket, and observed KV cache hit class. The fingerprint is intentionally low-cardinality (target: < 10k active cohorts) and stable across retries.
- Emits two new metrics per invocation: scenario_id (label), per_invocation_token_cost_us (microseconds-per-token equivalent), and spectral_cost_vector (a small 4-bin spectrum that summarizes token-cost distribution across the first N tokens). Metrics are emitted via our existing telemetry pipeline (metric name prefixes telemetry.inv.scenario.*) with aggregation-friendly labels.
- Implements a sampling service (spectral-anchor-sampler) in observability/ingest that performs reservoir sampling on scenario cohorts to store representative spectral vectors and a short example trace per cohort. This enables low-cost storage of cohort exemplars for dive-in analysis.
- Adds a Grafana dashboard (dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json) with: scenario cohort heatmap, spectral anchor gallery (exemplar traces), per-scenario P50/P95 cost lines, and a cohort drift sparkline.
- Adds an adaptive alert: if a scenario's spectral centroid shifts by more than a configured threshold AND its per-invocation cost increases by > 15% for a rolling hour and the scenario frequency > 0.05% of traffic, open a Severity-2 incident for investigation (tuning defaults provided).
- Documentation: new docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md describing how to interpret cohorts, tuning knobs, and migration notes.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- The scenario fingerprint code lives in runtime/ingress/profile.py and is feature-flag guarded with config: observability.scenario_profiling.enabled (default: off for private deployments; on for hosted beta).
- To avoid high-cardinality issues we cap unique scenario labels via hashing into a fixed bucket space and expose a telemetry.inv.scenario.bucket label. High-cardinality clients will see collisions but sampling retains exemplar traces for dominant traffic shapes.
- spectral_cost_vector is a compact string-encoded histogram (base64 of 4 bytes) to keep metric cardinality low; downstream processing decodes it into a 4-bin vector. The choice of 4 bins was an empirical tradeoff between expressiveness and metric cardinality.
- Storage for exemplar traces is limited to one exemplar per cohort per 24h by the sampler; retention is driven by observability.sampler.retention_days (default 7).

Commits (summary):
- Add scenario fingerprint generator and unit tests (runtime/ingress/profile.py) (+58/-3)
- Emit scenario metrics at ingress and enrich span tags (telemetry/emitter.py) (+104/-12)
- Add spectral-anchor-sampler microservice and reservoir implementation (observability/sampler/) (+168/-24)
- Grafana dashboard and small dashboard utils (dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json, dashboards/utils) (+42/-0)
- Docs and runbook (docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md) (+49/-3)

Changed areas (high-level):
- runtime/ingress/profile.py: new profiler and unit tests
- telemetry/emitter.py: metric emission points and labels
- observability/sampler/: new service that runs alongside metric ingest processors
- dashboards/observability/invocation_scenarios.json: dashboard panels and layout
- docs/observability/invocation-scenarios.md: user guide and alert tuning notes

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint stability across small perturbations to prompts.
- Integration test that simulates 10k synthetic scenarios and verifies sampler retains exemplars for top-k cohorts and falls back cleanly when bucket collisions occur.
- E2E in staging: load test with 100k invocations/hour to validate that metric cardinality growth is bounded and that the sampler memory footprint remains stable (observed < 150MB).
- Dashboard smoke tests added to ci/grafana-smoke.sh to assert panel JSON loads and basic queries return non-empty results.

Review conversation (high level):
- Mateo Ruiz: "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add an operator-friendly circuit-breaker so the sampler can be torn down if it starts to thrash; (2) make alert thresholds configurable via cluster-level config maps."
- Asha Patel (author): "Added sampler.enable circuit breaker and configmap-driven thresholds. Put defaults in config/observability.yaml; documented in the runbook."
- Grace Li: "Can we avoid base64 string for spectral vector — tough to query in sub-second dashboards?"
- Asha: "We keep the base64 for metric emission to avoid cardinality explosion; the sampler stores decoded vectors in exemplars which the dashboard queries separately. Added note to docs explaining the two-step decode flow."
- Oliver Bennett: "Please add a short hotfix plan if a cohort alert floods SRE."
- Asha: "Added runbook section and a quick CLI to mute a scenario cohort via 'rbacctl obs mute-scenario <bucket>' which SRE can use."

CI status: CI initially failed on lint (line length in docs) and one flaky grafana-smoke test. After fixes: lint and grafana smoke pass, unit & integration tests pass, e2e staging validated.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated rollout: enable for 10% of hosted traffic for one week, monitor SLI for metric ingestion lag and sampler memory.
2) Gradually increase to 50% and then full rollout if no regressions.
3) For Dedicated/Private customers the feature is off by default; on request we enable in a controlled beta with config guidance.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- All changes are additive; no schema changes to existing metrics. Dashboards are optional. If the sampler is not enabled, nothing is stored beyond emitted metrics.

Operational notes:
- Expected steady-state metric cardinality increase: +0.8% in medium clusters (measured in staging).
- Sampler memory usage: ~1–2MB per active cohort. Defaults limit cohorts to the top 2k by frequency to bound memory.
- If an alert floods, operators can mute by cohort bucket via rbacctl or scale down sampler replicas.

Why this is valuable:
This PR gives SRE and Product teams a practical way to find actionable cohorts driving cost and latency regressions — not just signal on aggregate percentiles. The spectral anchors provide compact exemplars that make investigating root cause (prompt shape, model variant, or routing policy) much faster than chasing noisy percentiles.

Follow-ups:
- Add lightweight per-cohort A/B comparison panels to measure quality regressions aligned with cost drift (ENG-2214).
- Explore automated remediation playbooks that propose route-policy fallbacks when a high-frequency scenario becomes expensive.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main by Asha Patel on 2026-02-25 after green CI and successful staging validation.
